docs.title: 3 · Hello, TestLab: your first test, by hand
docs.text: Goal: write one small test yourself, see it pass, then see it fail. No AI yet. Time: 15 minutes

docs.title: The service you test
docs.text:
The hello service is a tiny API. Its address is in box B of your handout.

Call Answers GET /hello {"message": "Hello, Tractus-X!"} GET /parts The parts P-1001 and P-1002 GET /parts/{partId} That part, or 404 GET /health {"status": "UP"} Full specification (OpenAPI) 
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Hello service
  version: "1.0.0"
  description: >
    A tiny read-only API for the first test of the Eclipse Tractus-X E2E testing
    tutorial. It says hello and knows two parts. Every answer is JSON, errors
    included.
  license:
    name: Apache-2.0
    url: https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
servers:
  - url: /
paths:
  /hello:
    get:
      summary: Say hello
      operationId: sayHello
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The greeting.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Greeting" }
              example: { message: "Hello, Tractus-X!" }
  /parts:
    get:
      summary: List the parts
      operationId: listParts
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Every part the service knows.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/PartSummary" }
  /parts/{partId}:
    get:
      summary: Read one part
      operationId: getPart
      parameters:
        - name: partId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: { type: string, example: P-1001 }
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The part.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Part" }
              example: { partId: P-1001, name: Brake disc, manufacturerPartId: BD-4711, weightKg: 7.2 }
        "404":
          description: No part with this id.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem" }
  /health:
    get:
      summary: Is the service up?
      operationId: health
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The service is up.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  status: { type: string, example: UP }
components:
  schemas:
    Greeting:
      type: object
      required: [message]
      properties:
        message: { type: string }
    PartSummary:
      type: object
      required: [partId, name]
      properties:
        partId: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
    Part:
      type: object
      required: [partId, name, manufacturerPartId, weightKg]
      properties:
        partId: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        manufacturerPartId: { type: string }
        weightKg: { type: number }
    Problem:
      type: object
      required: [status, title]
      properties:
        status: { type: integer }
        title: { type: string }
        detail: { type: string }

Not at the workshop? Run it with Docker as its README shows, at http://localhost:8080.

docs.title: The test
docs.text:
tests/says_hello.yaml
kind: test
syntax: v1-alpha

namespace: hello-e2e
id: says-hello

metadata:
  name: "The service says hello"
  version: "v0.1.0"
  description: Calls GET /hello and checks the greeting.

execution:
  - id: say_hello
    uses: http/http_request
    name: Ask the service to say hello
    with:
      url: "${{ env.service_url }}/hello"
    returns:
      status_code:
        type: integer
      body:
        type: object
    validate:
      - uses: validate/assert
        with: { input: status_code, operator: equals, value: 200 }
      - uses: validate/field
        with: { input: body, path: message, operator: equals, value: "Hello, Tractus-X!" }
  • uses picks the action: one HTTP request.
  • with gives its inputs. ${{ env.service_url }} is the address, taken from the manifest.
  • returns names the outputs you check.
  • validate holds the checks. The step passes only if all of them hold.

The syntax cheat sheet explains every part.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
VS CodeTest Suite IDE

  1. Install TestLab (Python 3.12+) and the VS Code extension YAML by Red Hat:

    pip install "tractusx-testlab==1.0.0a24"

  2. Unpack hello-start.zip into a folder hello and open it in VS Code.

  3. In index.yaml, set service_url to the address on your handout.

  4. Create tests/says_hello.yaml with the test above. Its first line turns on autocomplete:

    # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eclipse-tractusx/tractusx-testlab/v1-alpha24/src/tractusx_testlab/compiler/schemas/tck_test.schema.json

  5. In index.yaml, replace tests: [] with:

    tests:
  - id: says_hello.yaml
    name: The service says hello

  6. Run:

    testlab validate index.yaml
testlab run index.yaml --yes
  1. Open the Test Suite (box B) and click the Test Suite IDE icon on the left.

  2. Click Open File and choose hello-start.zip.

  3. ☰ → Environment → Variables → service_url: enter the address on your handout.

  4. New ▾ → New Test, then click new-test.yaml.

  5. Open the YAML Editor at the right edge, click Edit, paste the test, click Save. The blocks appear.

  6. Click Compile, then Run. Save the draft, and click Run again if it does not start. Pick any app under test (or Register an app), click Next to the end, then Run.

More on every button: The Test Suite IDE.

RESULT: PASS  |  1 passed  0 failed  0 skipped

docs.title: Make it fail
docs.text:
1. Change the expected greeting to Hello, world! and run. It fails with Expected 'Hello, world!', got 'Hello, Tractus-X!'.
  2. Change it back. Green again.

docs.title: Your turn
docs.text:
Write tests/unknown_part_is_not_found.yaml: ask for part P-9999, expect 404. Register it and run.

Solution tests/unknown_part_is_not_found.yaml
kind: test
syntax: v1-alpha

namespace: hello-e2e
id: unknown-part-is-not-found

metadata:
  name: "An unknown part is not found"
  version: "v0.1.0"
  description: Negative test. Asks for a part the service does not know.

execution:
  - id: read_unknown_part
    uses: http/http_request
    name: Ask for a part that does not exist
    with:
      url: "${{ env.service_url }}/parts/P-9999"
    returns:
      status_code:
        type: integer
    validate:
      - uses: validate/assert
        with: { input: status_code, operator: equals, value: 404 }
More time? Check the shape of a part tests/reads_a_part.yaml
kind: test
syntax: v1-alpha

namespace: hello-e2e
id: reads-a-part

metadata:
  name: "A part has the shape the specification promises"
  version: "v0.1.0"
  description: Contract test. Reads part P-1001 and checks it against the Part schema.

execution:
  - id: read_part
    uses: http/http_request
    name: Read part P-1001
    with:
      url: "${{ env.service_url }}/parts/P-1001"
    returns:
      status_code:
        type: integer
      body:
        type: object
    validate:
      - uses: validate/assert
        with: { input: status_code, operator: equals, value: 200 }
      - uses: validate/field
        with: { input: body, path: name, operator: equals, value: "Brake disc" }
      - uses: validate/schema
        with: { input: body, schema: "${{ env.schemas.part }}" }

The finished project is in examples/hello.

Tip

Stuck? YAML error: check the indentation (two spaces, no tabs). Service unreachable: open <address>/health in the browser. No blocks in the IDE: click Save in the YAML editor.

docs.text: Getting Started · chapter 4, route B · ● ● ● ● ○ ○ ○ ○ ○

docs.title: 4B · Connect a local model
docs.text:
Goal: a model on your own laptop answers you in the IDE. Time: 10 minutes, plus the download

The model runs on your laptop, so nothing leaves your machine. The IDE's Small model mode gives it short instructions and lets it look up what it needs, so even a small model answers in seconds.

docs.title: Which model?
docs.text:
Your laptop Take Download 8 GB of RAM qwen2.5:3b 2 GB 16 GB of RAM qwen2.5:3b or qwen2.5:7b 2 or 5 GB 32 GB or more, Apple Silicon or a large GPU A larger model, for example qwen2.5:14b or qwen3:30b 9 to 18 GB

In our trial, qwen2.5:3b and qwen2.5:7b both made every change the tutorial needs. Take the 3B unless your laptop has room to spare. The larger ones we have not tried. On a laptop without a GPU, expect a minute per step: route A or C is the better choice there.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Ollama.

  2. Download the model. Best at home, before the session:

    ollama pull qwen2.5:3b

  3. Start Ollama so that the IDE may call it. Put the address from box B of your handout in place of the example:

    OLLAMA_ORIGINS="https://ide.example.org" OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve

  4. Download the template, e2e-test-template.zip.

  5. In the IDE you used in chapter 3, click ☰, then File, then File or package, and choose the ZIP.
  6. At the top right, click Ask AI. Under Model, choose Local / self-hosted LLM. Keep Server at Ollama and click Connect.
  7. Choose your model in the list. Leave Small model mode switched on.
  8. Type Hello. What is in this project? and press Enter.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text: After step 8, the assistant answers with a short description of the two tests, within half a minute.

docs.title: How to talk to a small model
docs.text:
You will use these in chapter 5:

  • One change per message. "Rename the step", then "add a check". Not "write the test".
  • Name the file every time: In tests/partner_uses_my_product.yaml …. Each message stands alone; the model does not remember the previous one.
  • Read every change. Each one is listed above the message box with Review and Undo.

Note

Small model mode is new. If your IDE does not show the switch yet, a local model needs OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 and a fast machine, and the first answer takes minutes. Then take route A or C.

Tip

Stuck?

  • "Could not load the server's models": Ollama is not running, or the address in OLLAMA_ORIGINS is not exactly the IDE's address. Stop it and start it again (step 3).
  • It answers but never changes a file: you are in Ask or Plan. Switch to Agent.
  • It keeps getting it wrong: ask for a smaller change, or switch to route A or C.

docs.title: 4C · Build with your own AI tool
docs.text:
Goal: a test project for your product that compiles, built on your laptop with the AI coding assistant you already have. Time: 20 minutes. It replaces chapters 4 and 5.

Take this route when you have no API key for the assistant in the IDE, but you do have an assistant of your own: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Cursor, Codex or a chat app. A subscription is enough here, because you use the vendor's own tool.

The assistant does not know the TCK format. The agent kit teaches it: a skill with the syntax, the patterns, the template and a review checklist. Expect a little less comfort than in the IDE. It works.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install the TestLab command line. Your assistant uses it to check its own work:

    pip install "tractusx-testlab==1.0.0a24"

  2. Clone the fork you made in chapter 2 and start a branch:

    git clone https://github.com/<your-user>/<your-product>.git
cd <your-product>
git switch -c test/e2e-test

  3. Get the tutorial's files next to it, and install the skill for your tool. Use claude, copilot, cursor or codex:

    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/eclipse-tractusx/tutorial-resources.git ../tutorial-resources
../tutorial-resources/e2e-testing/agent-kit/install.sh claude

    Another tool, or a chat app? See Set up your AI tool.

  4. Copy the template into your repository:

    mkdir -p tck .github/workflows
cp -R ../tutorial-resources/e2e-testing/template/tck/e2e tck/e2e

  5. Open the repository folder in your assistant, start a new chat and send this, with your product and the scenario from the handout, box A:

    Use the tractusx-e2e-test skill.

My product is "<product name>" (<repository URL>).
The test must prove: "<the scenario>"
The project is in tck/e2e. It is the template: turn it into this test.
Show me your plan first and wait for my yes.

  6. Read the plan. The Skeptic asks: does each test prove a promise, is the negative test a real refusal, and is nothing from the handout written into a file? Correct it in plain words, then say yes.

  7. Let the assistant write. It runs testlab validate after every file. When it says it is done, check for yourself:

    testlab validate tck/e2e/index.yaml
testlab compile tck/e2e/index.yaml -o /tmp/e2e-test.tck

  8. Open the IDE: the address and the account are in box B of your handout. Click the TestLab IDE icon in the bar on the left.

  9. On the welcome screen, click Open Folder and choose the folder tck/e2e of your repository.
  10. Press Compile.

Now continue with chapter 6. In chapter 7, skip steps 1, 2, 3 and 5: your files are already in your repository, with their licence headers.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
In the terminal:

OK — index.yaml is valid (no issues)

In the IDE, your tests in the explorer on the left and the message Compilation passed.

Note

You changed something in the IDE afterwards? Then the IDE has the newest version, not your folder. Export it as in chapter 7, step 1, and unpack it over tck/e2e. The export drops comments, so add the licence headers again as in chapter 7, step 5.

Tip

Stuck?

  • The assistant does not seem to know the skill: start a new chat, or point it at the file: Read ../tutorial-resources/e2e-testing/agent-kit/AGENTS.md and follow it.
  • It invents steps: say Use only steps that testlab docs lists.
  • testlab is not found: the pip install went into another Python. Try python3 -m pip install "tractusx-testlab==1.0.0a24" and open a new terminal.
  • validate stays red after three rounds: copy the template again (step 4) and ask for one test at a time.
  • Your assistant cannot run commands: run testlab validate yourself and paste the output back to it.

docs.text: Getting Started · chapter 5 of 9 · ● ● ● ● ● ○ ○ ○ ○

docs.title: 5 · Build the test with the assistant
docs.text:
Goal: a test project for your product that compiles. Time: 15 minutes

You say what must be proven. The assistant writes how. The Skeptic reads every line.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Press Compile at the top. The template compiles as it is: you start from green.
  2. In the assistant panel, switch the mode to Plan. A plan changes nothing.

  3. Paste starter prompt 1 and fill in your product, its repository and the scenario from the handout, box A. Send it.

    Your product has an E2E spec? Attach its raw spec file and send the prompt from part 8 of the spec instead. The plan then follows the spec. 4. Read the plan. The Skeptic asks three questions:

    Question A good plan says Does each test prove a promise? What the partner gets, not just "status 200" Is the negative test really a refusal? The exact answer the product must give Are addresses and BPNs variables? Nothing from your handout appears in a test

  4. Correct the plan in plain words until you agree with it.

  5. Press Carry out this plan. The assistant switches to Agent and writes the files.
  6. In the bar Changes by the AI assistant, press Review and read what changed. Undo file and Undo all put things back.
  7. Press Compile.

  8. Not green? Send this, and repeat until it is:

    Compile the project and fix what the compiler reports. Change nothing else.

  9. Press Save, give the draft your product's name, and press Save draft.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
The message Compilation passed, and your tests in the explorer on the left.

What the pilot team built Three tests for the Digital Twin Registry: | Test | Kind | | --- | --- | | A registered twin can be read back and matches the AAS schema | Positive, contract | | A partner finds and reads the twin through the owner's connector | Positive, the journey | | A twin that does not exist is answered with 404 | Negative | Read them in the [worked example](../reference/worked-example.md).

Note

On route B, with a local model: send one change per message and name the file in each one, for example In tests/partner_uses_my_product.yaml rename the step call_product to "Partner calls my product". A whole test in one message is too much for a small model.

Tip

Stuck?

  • The assistant invents steps: say Use only steps from the block catalog.
  • Compile stays red after three rounds: switch to Ask, paste the finding and ask what the compiler expects there, before you let it edit again.
  • Minute 30 and still red, or no model at all: press Undo all and change only the names by hand. Click a file, open the YAML Editor tab, press Edit, replace my-product with your product's id and My Product with its name, and press Save. Do it in index.yaml and in both tests. A small green test beats a large red one.
  • More prompts: Starter prompts.

docs.title: 6 · Run it against your connectors
docs.text: Goal: a green run, and one red run that you caused on purpose. Time: 10 minutes

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Press Run at the top. The dialog Run to debug opens with five steps.

    Step You do Build Nothing. It ends with "Compiled — ready to run." Press Next. Infrastructure Choose your product under App under test and your connector under EDC Connector. If your test uses a registry, choose it under Digital Twin Registry. Press Next. Variables Click each value in the list. Fill in what is empty from box C of your handout: product_internal_url is "Product, as the connector reaches it", dtr_internal_url is "Registry, as the connector reaches it". Where the dialog offers a list, choose from it. Press Next. SUT Setup Press Start review, then Accept all and Confirm all. Your test creates these offers itself, in its setup. Press Next. Summary & Launch Check the list of tests. Press Run at the bottom right.

    You type nothing from box D. The partner side is set up by the administrators.

  2. Watch the Console at the bottom. Each step turns green or red as it finishes.

  3. Wait for the result.
  4. Now break it on purpose. Open your negative test, change the expected value of one check, for example 0 to 1 or 404 to 200, and run again.
  5. See it turn red at that check. Change it back and run once more.

A test that has never failed has proven nothing yet. Step 4 is the difference between a test and a script that prints green.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
The last step of the dialog, with your tests and your connector listed, and after the run the status Passed.

The second step, Infrastructure, looks like this when your components are registered:

Note

Nothing to choose under Infrastructure? Register it yourself, with the values of box C: Register an app (name and version of your product), Register a connector (name, DSP URL, Participant ID and DID) and Register a registry (name and base URL).

Tip

Stuck?

  • The run fails at once with "requires infrastructure that is not fully bound: engine.connector": the partner side is not set up for your team. Go to the Desk.
  • The run waits: give it a minute, then ask at the Desk whether your connectors are up.
  • A value is refused as "not a public host name": use the address from box C exactly as printed.
  • A step is red: open it and read the request and the answer. Decide which it is:
    • The environment. Nothing answered, or a value is wrong. Fix the value or ask.
    • A finding. The product answered, and not as your check expects. Either your reading of the promise is wrong, or the product is. Both are worth knowing.
  • Minute 40 and no green run: go on to chapter 7. The workflow runs your test again in CI, in a dataspace of its own.

docs.title: 7 · Add it to your repository
docs.text: Goal: your test and the workflow that runs it are committed on a branch of your fork. Time: 10 minutes

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the IDE, click the ☰ menu at the top right, then File, then Export. In the dialog, press Export ZIP. The file lands in your downloads folder, named after your project.

  2. Open a terminal and clone the fork you made in chapter 2:

    git clone https://github.com/<your-user>/<your-product>.git
cd <your-product>
git switch -c test/e2e-test

  3. Unpack the ZIP into the folder tck/e2e:

    mkdir -p tck/e2e .github/workflows
unzip ~/Downloads/<your-project>.zip -d tck/e2e

  4. Add the workflow. It is the same for every product:

    BASE=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eclipse-tractusx/tutorial-resources/main/e2e-testing
curl -fsSL "$BASE/examples/digital-twin-registry/.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml" -o .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml

  5. In the same terminal, add the licence header to your test files. Eclipse projects need it on every file, and the IDE's export does not write it:

    curl -fsSL "$BASE/template/license-header.txt" -o /tmp/license-header.txt
for f in $(find tck/e2e -name '*.yaml'); do
  cat /tmp/license-header.txt "$f" > "$f.new" && mv "$f.new" "$f"
done

  6. Commit, with a sign-off:

    git add tck .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml
git commit -s -m "test: add an E2E test"

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
git show --stat HEAD

    test: add an E2E test

    Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.org>

 .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml               |  44 ++++
 tck/e2e/index.yaml                           | ...
 tck/e2e/tests/<your-first-test>.yaml         | ...
 tck/e2e/tests/<your-second-test>.yaml        | ...

And this is all the workflow is: a few lines that call a reusable workflow.

Tip

Stuck?

  • curl answers 404: the tutorial is not published at that address yet. Ask a facilitator for the address to use, also for the uses: line of the workflow file.
  • No unzip on your machine: unpack the ZIP with your file manager and move index.yaml and tests into tck/e2e.
  • Your repository already has a folder tck/e2e: choose another folder, and change tck-directory in the workflow file to match.
  • Your product does not run in the developer toolbox: open .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml and add run-in-toolbox: false under tck-directory. The workflow then validates and compiles only. See The workflow.
  • Signed-off-by is missing: you forgot -s. Run git commit --amend -s --no-edit.

docs.title: 8 · Link it and open the pull request
docs.text: Goal: a draft pull request in your product's repository, with the test linked in .tractusx. Time: 5 minutes

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the file .tractusx in the root of your repository. It is the metafile that describes the product.

  2. Add this block at the end, with your product's name:

    e2eTests:
  - name: "<Your product> E2E test"
    path: "tck/e2e"
    workflow: ".github/workflows/e2e-test.yml"

  3. Commit and push:

    git add .tractusx
git commit -s -m "chore: link the E2E test in the metafile"
git push -u origin test/e2e-test

  4. Open your fork on GitHub. Press Compare & pull request in the yellow banner.

  5. Check that the base repository is eclipse-tractusx/<your-product>. Write one sentence per test: what it proves.
  6. Open the arrow next to the green button, choose Create draft pull request and press it.
  7. Ring the bell.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
Your pull request, with the checks starting at the bottom: Validate and compile finishes in under a minute, Run in Eclipse Tractus-X developer toolbox in about five.

Click the second job and scroll to E2E test result. This is the pilot team's:

TCK RUN SUMMARY
  ✓ Register and read                          PASS
  ✓ A partner reads through the connector      PASS
  ✓ An unknown twin is not found               PASS
RESULT: PASS  |  3 passed  0 failed  0 skipped

Note

The first contribution of a person to a repository needs a committer's approval before its workflows run. If your checks say waiting for approval, that is the reason, not an error. A facilitator knows who can approve.

Tip

Stuck?

  • You want to see it run now: open a second pull request inside your fork, from test/e2e-test to your fork's main. It needs no approval and runs at once.
  • The ECA check is red: the email of your commits is not the one of your Eclipse account. See Troubleshooting.
  • git push is refused: GitHub wants a token or an SSH key, not your password. Let a teammate whose laptop can push be the Driver.
  • A check fails: Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 4 · Choose your AI
docs.text:
Goal: pick the AI help that fits your laptop and what you brought. Time: 1 minute

There are three routes. They all end in the same place: a test project that compiles, ready for chapter 6. Not sure? Take A if you have a key, otherwise C if you have an AI coding tool, otherwise B.

  • A · An API key in the IDE

    You have a key from OpenAI, Anthropic or Catena-X AI. Fastest, and the best results.

    You need: the key. Time: 5 + 15 minutes.

    Take route A →

  • B · A local model in the IDE

    The model runs on your own laptop. No key, and nothing leaves your machine. Good for small, clear changes.

    You need: Ollama and 8 GB of RAM or more. Time: 10 + 20 minutes.

    Take route B →

  • C · Your own AI tool, then upload

    You build on your laptop with Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor or Codex, then open the result in the IDE. A subscription is enough.

    You need: your tool and Python. Time: 20 minutes.

    Take route C →
